chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: Oliver's gum trouble, mutes and plunger
summary: Oliver's pyorrhea forced him to use extra trumpeters and soft muted playing; Moore says he was first to use a bottle as a wah-wah mute.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, how was he playing at that time, in your estimation? I mean, was he starting to show some of the physical problems with his gums or with his embrochure that were to really hamper him very late in life?

That's when he come to have three or four more, extra trumpet players, because he couldn't make, couldn't play... He had other guys playing for him. He had a guy like Henry "Red" Allen, Louis Metcalf on some of them, and Ward Pinkett on some of them. Because he had what call pyorrhea.
Yeah, the gums. His teeth were practically all gone. He would get this... He just brushed it off, and so ...(?)...(?)... When he started making them notes, he couldn't make them.

When he did play, he'd play real soft. But he liked to play with the mutes, what you call mutes in his horn. You put a mute in your horn, keep it soft. And he played some stuff in that wah-wah thing, with the glass...

Yeah, the glass. He had a Coca-Cola bottle he'd put in there, and he'd take it, pull it up and down like that, use it as a plunger. He was the first person that I heard do that. I heard a record a long time ago of a
fellow named Johnny Dunn, who used to play all that stuff, the wah-wah. And the next one was Cootie Williams.
Oh yeah. When Cootie would do it, he would get a growl.
